entries.title: Debate can list the papers citing an article
entries.body: For an article you added, when it has a DOI whose record matches it, the Reception part of Debate has a Cited by list: the citation count from OpenAlex, a public index of scholarly work, and up to 100 citing works, ten shown at first. It appears without starting the paid Debate search and uses no AI. The privacy page names OpenAlex, Crossref and DataCite.

entries.title: Recall questions can carry a hidden hint
entries.body: When Recall asks whether you remember something, it is asked to link the passage that answers the question and to add a hint, kept behind a Hint button until you want it. The hint is meant to point towards the answer rather than give it; neither the link nor the hint is guaranteed every time. Copying an answer includes the hint only while it is open.

entries.title: Papers dated only by year show that year
entries.body: When a paper's record gives a year but no exact day, its Metadata page shows the year, as in "Published 2011", and so does your library, which sorts it at the start of that year. Visitors to an article you have made public also see its journal and publication date, where known.

entries.title: DOIs joined to web addresses are read correctly
entries.body: In some PDFs a web address is printed straight after the DOI with no space between them. The two were read as one, so the paper got no journal, publication date or DOI. The DOI is now read on its own.
